findings.title: Silence action is broken when only a promRule is supplied (new Grafana alert list view)
findings.body: RuleActionsButtons now accepts either `rule` (RulerRuleDTO) or `promRule` (Rule), but the Silence drawer is only mounted when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true: `{rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer && (<SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer rulerRule={rule} .../>)}`. GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx (used by GrafanaGroupLoader and FilterView, i.e. the whole new alert list) only passes `promRule`, never `rule`. Meanwhile AlertRuleMenu's `canSilence` is computed from the Grafana-prom-based ability check and can be true for these promRule-only invocations, so the 'Silence notifications' menu item is rendered and clickable (confirmed by GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx which asserts the silence menu item is present). Clicking it calls `handleSilence` → `setShowSilenceDrawer(true)`, but because `rule` is always undefined in this flow, the guard `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is always false and the drawer never renders. Users will see a Silence option that does nothing when clicked, with no error or feedback.

findings.title: Missing `key` prop when rendering GrafanaRuleListItem in a list
findings.body: In the `rules.map(...)` loop, the previous `<GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} .../>` is replaced with `<GrafanaRuleListItem rule={rule} groupIdentifier={groupIdentifier} namespaceName={...} showLocation={true} />` without a `key` prop. The other two branches of the same switch (`DataSourceRuleLoader` and `UnknownRuleListItem`) still pass `key={key}`. Rendering a list item without a stable key causes React reconciliation issues (console warnings, and potential incorrect DOM/component reuse) especially problematic here since this view implements infinite scroll where the `rules` array grows incrementally.

findings.title: Rule view link no longer carries the `returnTo` parameter
findings.body: The previous implementation (removed GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx) built the rule link with `createRelativeUrl(\`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view\`, { returnTo })` where `returnTo` was computed via `createReturnTo()`. The new GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx drops this entirely: `href: createRelativeUrl(\`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view\`)`. This removes the 'return to previous page' functionality when a user clicks a rule from the alert list (e.g. from a filtered search), so after viewing/editing the rule, the user can no longer be navigated back to the exact list/filter state they came from.

findings.title: New `provenance` field on GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase has no accompanying backend change in this PR
findings.body: `isProvisionedPromRule()` (utils/rules.ts) and the new `GrafanaRuleListItem`/`useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` logic rely on `promRule.provenance` to gate Edit/Delete/Pause abilities for provisioned (locked) rules. This PR adds `provenance?: string` to `GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase` but contains no Go backend changes (no files under the Go backend are part of this PR). If the Grafana Prometheus rules API (`/api/prometheus/grafana/api/v1/rules`) does not already populate this field, `provenance` will always be `undefined` for promRule-only consumers, causing `isProvisionedPromRule` to always return false — meaning provisioned/locked Grafana rules could incorrectly appear editable/deletable from the new alert list view.

findings.title: Pause and Delete actions silently become unreachable for promRule-only consumers, with no documentation of the limitation
findings.body: `MenuItemPauseRule` (line ~123) is only rendered when `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` is true, and the Delete menu item (line ~165) requires `rulerRule` truthy. Since the new alert list view flow (GrafanaRuleListItem → RuleActionsButtons.V2 → AlertRuleMenu) never supplies a `rulerRule`, Pause and Delete are now permanently absent from the dropdown menu for rules shown in that view, even though the corresponding `canPause`/`canDelete` abilities can be computed as true via the Grafana-prom-based ability checks. This is a real functional regression/limitation (confirmed by GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx asserting exactly 4 menu items with no mention of Pause/Delete), but it is not called out anywhere in the PR description or code comments, risking confusion for future maintainers or being perceived as an unintentional regression.

findings.title: Menu item presence tests don't verify the actual Silence action functionality
findings.body: The test 'should render correct menu actions when More button is clicked' only checks that the Silence, Copy link, Duplicate and Export menu items are present (`ui.menuItems.silence().get()`, etc.) but never clicks the Silence item to assert that the SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer actually opens. This test gap allowed the regression where the Silence menu item renders but produces no visible effect (see RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx finding) to go undetected.
